description: Newcastle's LIVE-STATE documentation claims - the CITY-OWNED half of tests/check_doc_currency.py. Each entry pins one number written into a document to the artefact that decides it, so a figure cannot silently outlive the thing it describes. A second city supplies its own copy at cities/<city>/tests/doc_currency.json; the harness in tests/ names no city, no document and no number.
what_belongs_here: ONLY live-state cells - a table row or sentence that must equal the artefact TODAY. A dated record is frozen and must never be claimed: DECISIONS.md 14 saying 'manifest 436' on 24 August is history, and STATUS.md's dated task rows are the same. Claiming a record would force the project to rewrite its own past to keep a check green, which is the exact opposite of the reproducibility rule.
why_these_two_documents: README.md is the front door and STATUS.md is the board - both are long-lived, both are read for current state, and both drifted. NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md is deliberately absent: /handoff rewrites it wholesale every session, so pinned patterns there would break by design and train readers to ignore the check. The brief's numbers are covered because /handoff sources them from STATUS.md, which is checked.
